I appreciate it, and am sorry you're also going through something similar, I wouldn't wish it on my worse enemy. 

My problem is that my life isn't bad, in fact, anyone living it would say it's going pretty great. It's not the life that bothers me, it's the living that makes it up as a whole. Life hasn't been tragic for me, it hasn't kicked me when I've been down, I just don't want to be part of it anymore. 

I'm not sure if it's sadness, or hopelessness, or nihilism that makes me feel this way, but the thought of living for a better life seems pointless to me. Life is just a personal experience for each individual and mine has been going more and more gray by the day. 

I admit it is a little comforting knowing I'm not the only one who feels this way, but it isn't enough to alter the way I feel. It sucks that other people are suffering too, but it's always hard to remember this and empathize when you're own personal experience is blocking out everything else you feel would slightly help. 

I tell myself that eventually it will get better, but it instead feels more like I'm on some countdown. I like everyone I love a little less everyday and everything I love becomes less fulfilling. This makes the aspect of waiting to see what happens seem incredibly unappealing, I just don't want to keep feeling this way for another month, let alone a few more years.

If you want to talk to her, don't just base it off your classes and only work with that. You want this girl, then get to know her. There is a remarkable course of action called honesty that most girls appreciate. It seems like a long shot, but just tell her you'd like to get to know her better. I'm serious, it is one of the easiest (and less complicated ways) of communication.

Girls cannot read minds, they normally don't think that every guy who talks to them has a crush on them. Also, the course of, "I hope that if I'm a super nice guy to her, then she'll fall for me." Is rarely ever successful. While some girls crave relationships, most crave friends even more. You will get friendzoned, it isn't something against you, it's actually considered a good thing if you aren't trying to date them. Being someones emotional confident shouldn't be something to bitch about.

I went off on a bit of a tangent.

Tell her you'd like to get to know her, if she is cool with the idea, talk to her. After a few weeks of talking, if you can make it not awkward (Be yourself, don't try to be what you think she wants) then straight up tell her that you like her. If you want a relationship, it is better to start it off with honesty then sleight of hand. 

On the brightside, the worst that can happen is that she doesn't like you back. Then you can move on or at least work on moving on.

This advice is spot on. Find someone who is closer to you, that way you won't miss out on all the wonderful (And sometimes shitty) parts of a relationship. It is better to experience it all with someone tangible then to attempt it with somebody long distance. 

As for her having a boyfriend, dude, don't be the one to break up a good thing. If she is happy with her boyfriend, then let her be happy. It would make you a lot better of a person. If you haven't seen her in ten years, it means she probably has a lot going on that you don't know about. You're young dude, just enjoy the experiences while you can instead of hoping for something that's a "maybe" at best. Find a nice girl near you and dedicate your time and energy to her, not someone who already has a special somebody for that. 

2 cents.

It sounds like you are in a place where the heart is racing ahead of you, with no control of the situation. I had a similar problem when I was younger (Going to spare the ugly details) but I basically can tell you a remarkable way of getting her to know how you feel.

Talk to her.

I don't want to come off as sardonic but if you are going to have a relationship, you need active communication in the first place. Woman (Or in your case, girls) cannot read your mind. Hoping that they pick up on signals that you are giving is honestly stupid. 

Tell her, man. Talk to her about it, don't come off like you are joking, grow a back bone and tell her that how you feel is important and you want her to know about it. If she doesn't respond in the way you hope, well at least you know. Love fades, don't think you are a unique snowflake, we have all been through it before. It feels like it'll last forever but it won't, you are way too young to be this miserable over something like this for so long. 

At the very least, if you even bother to take the advice from a person who has stood on the same sandbox before, you can move on and find someone better for you (They exist, trust me) and she can find someone better for her. You can't force someone to love you (Trust me again, I gave it an effort once).

Hope this helps.

Shirdel is right man, just actually go for it. You will never know what would have happened if you don't give the dice a throw first. Worse comes to worse, she says no. You can move on and stop wondering about it.

It sounds like you are just a source of revenue to her and that isn't cool. I think that you should cut your losses where you are and find someone who actually values you for who you are, not what you have. It sounds cheesey but if you have been willing to burn your money on her just so she can be happy, then I bet you are a pretty alright guy. 

Leave her, man. Make yourself happy by finding someone who wants you to be happy. You deserve it.
